course_name_original: Basics of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer
course_name_en: Basics of Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer
prerequisites: CS-A1111 Basic Course in Programming Y1

learning_outcomes.text: Use of ideal gas and Van der Waals equations of state.
Calculation and interpretation of the compressibility factor.
Calculation and interpretation of the vapor quality factor.
Understanding the first law of thermodynamics.
Calculation of work, internal energy change, and heat along a process path.
Calculation of thermal efficiency for a cyclic process.
Understanding enthalpy and the energy balance of a steady flow process.
Calculation of thermal efficiency for power plant processes.
Understanding entropy and the second law of thermodynamics.
Definitions and use of fundamental relations to calculate the entropy change of an ideal gas.
Definitions and use of Gibbs and Helmholtz free energies to calculate state quantities.
Understanding the heat pump cycle and calculation of the COP coefficient.
Definition and use of isentropic efficiency in power plant and heat pump processes.
Use of Fourier's law in one dimension to determine temperature profile in a solid.
Determining the heat transfer coefficient in the case of several material layers for a plate-like element.
Evaluation of the convective heat transfer coefficient.
Analysing heat transfer through a solid material layer into a flowing fluid.
Radiation heat transfer between two surfaces and application to the analysis of a solar thermal collector.
